pr_title: Recover from previously failed statistics migrations
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The stats timestamp migration had some somewhat rare failure cases that were not accounted for:

- If a user has duplicate rows that were manually inserted or inserted by external stats before we had the unique index they could fail to migrate. We now fallback to a one by one migration when this happens.
- If the user downgraded HA from 2023.3.x to an older version without restoring the database and they upgrade again with the same database they will have un-migrated statistics columns since we only migrate them once.

Because this involves migrating data, this should go through beta. While it means the users in the linked issue will have to wait a month for a solution, we need to make sure it doesn't have any side effects.

I encountered this issue when updating to the 2023.10.x releases and ultimately downgraded to the 2023.9.x releases while waiting for this fix. I upgraded to 2023.11.0b5 to test this fix and encountered an issue with the migration. It appears that somehow my database contains duplicate records, with one record having the `start` column populated and`start_ts` null, a an otherwise duplicate record with `start` null and `start_ts` populated. As a result the migration failed due to a constraint violation on the index of `metadata_id` and `start_ts`.

I was able to "fix" the issue locally, by manually updating the start column to avoid null start values from resetting the `start_ts` value during migration. I did this on both the statistics and statistics_short_term tables with a query similar to:

```sql
update
	statistics_short_term set
	start = to_timestamp(start_ts)
where
	id in  
(
	select
		id
	from
		statistics_short_term  s1
	where
		start is null
		and start_ts is not null
		and start_ts > 0
		and (
		select
			count(start)
		from
			statistics_short_term s2
		where
			s2.metadata_id = s1.metadata_id
			and s2.start = to_timestamp(s1.start_ts)) = 0)
```

Once this was done I deleted the duplicate records (where `start` was still null after the above query). I did this with with a query similar to the following for both the statistics and statistics_short_term tables:

```sql
delete from statistics_short_term where id in 
(select
	id
from
	statistics_short_term s1
where
	s1.start_ts is null
	and s1.start is not null
	and 
s1.metadata_id in (
	select
		metadata_id
	from
		statistics_short_term s2
	where
		s2.metadata_id = s1.metadata_id
		and s2.start_ts = extract(EPOCH
	from
		s1.start::timestamptz))
		
)
```

I'm not sure if I ended up deleting more statistics than necessary, but after doing this the schema migration succeeded and things looked normal enough that if data was lost it wasn't important to me.
